definition_en: sudden and unexpected, often in an unpleasant way
example_en: The road came to an abrupt end at the edge of the cliff.
example_zh: 那条路在悬崖边戛然而止。

definition_en: a very large amount of something; how plentiful something is
example_en: The lake has an abundance of fish in early summer.
example_zh: 初夏时这个湖里鱼很多。

definition_en: existing in large amounts; more than enough
example_en: Sunlight is abundant in the desert all year round.
example_zh: 沙漠里一年四季阳光充足。

definition_en: to be next to something and touch it along one side
example_en: Their garden abuts a small public park.
example_zh: 他们的花园紧挨着一个小公园。

definition_en: to make something more noticeable
example_en: The dark frame accentuates the bright colors of the painting.
example_zh: 深色画框把画中明亮的颜色衬托得更突出。

definition_en: to praise someone or something publicly; strong public praise
example_en: Her first novel was acclaimed by critics around the world.
example_zh: 她的第一部小说受到世界各地评论家的赞誉。

definition_en: to provide enough space for something, or to adjust to fit a need
example_en: The schedule was changed to accommodate students who work in the evening.
example_zh: 为了照顾晚上要打工的学生，课表做了调整。

definition_en: in a way that suits the situation just described; as a result
example_en: The weather turned cold, and we dressed accordingly.
example_zh: 天气转冷，我们也相应地添了衣服。

definition_en: officially approved as meeting a required standard
definition_zh: 经官方认可的；获得资质的
example_en: She earned her degree from an accredited university.
example_zh: 她在一所有正式资质的大学取得了学位。

definition_en: to gradually increase in amount over time; to collect
example_en: Dust accumulates quickly on shelves that are never cleaned.
example_zh: 从不打扫的架子上很快就会积灰。

definition_en: containing acid; having a sour, sharp quality
example_en: Lemon juice is very acidic.
example_zh: 柠檬汁的酸性很强。

definition_en: the process of becoming more acidic
example_en: Ocean acidification makes it harder for shellfish to build their shells.
example_zh: 海洋酸化让贝类更难长出外壳。

definition_en: relating to sound or hearing; (of music) played without electric instruments
example_en: The hall was designed to have excellent acoustic qualities.
example_zh: 这个大厅在设计上追求出色的声学效果。

definition_en: a person you know, but who is not a close friend
example_en: He is not a friend, just an acquaintance from work.
example_zh: 他算不上朋友，只是工作上认识的人。

definition_en: to accept or agree to something without arguing, even if you do not want to
example_en: After a long discussion, she acquiesced to their request.
example_zh: 讨论了很久之后，她勉强同意了他们的请求。

definition_en: the act of getting or buying something
example_en: The museum announced the acquisition of three rare paintings.
example_zh: 博物馆宣布购得三幅珍贵的画作。

definition_en: in a way that is good enough for a particular purpose
example_en: The report does not adequately explain why the project failed.
example_zh: 这份报告没有充分说明项目为什么失败。

definition_en: to manage or give out something, such as a test, survey or medicine
example_en: The same test was administered to students in ten countries.
example_zh: 同一份测试在十个国家的学生中进行。

definition_en: very great love and admiration
example_en: The singer looked out at the crowd's faces, full of adoration.
example_zh: 歌手望着人群，一张张脸上满是崇拜。

definition_en: to publicly support an idea or a group; a person who does this
example_en: The group advocates for cleaner air in large cities.
example_zh: 这个团体呼吁改善大城市的空气质量。

definition_en: done from or happening in the air
example_en: Aerial photos showed how far the flood had spread.
example_zh: 航拍照片显示了洪水蔓延的范围。

definition_en: relating to beauty and how pleasing something looks or feels
example_en: The building was praised for its aesthetic appeal, not its usefulness.
example_zh: 这座建筑受到称赞是因为好看，而不是因为实用。

definition_en: to state firmly that something is true; to confirm
example_en: The new evidence affirms what the scientists had long suspected.
example_zh: 新的证据证实了科学家们长期以来的猜测。

definition_en: a group formed by many separate things or animals coming together
example_en: Large aggregations of butterflies gather in these trees every winter.
example_zh: 每年冬天都有大群蝴蝶聚集在这些树上。

definition_en: feeling angry or upset because you think you were treated unfairly
definition_zh: 感到委屈的；愤愤不平的
example_en: Aggrieved customers demanded their money back.
example_zh: 愤愤不平的顾客要求退款。

definition_en: to place in a straight line; to match or agree with something
example_en: The company's actions do not align with its stated values.
example_zh: 这家公司的做法和它宣称的价值观并不一致。

definition_en: to decide officially that something will be used for a particular purpose
example_en: The city allocated more money to public libraries this year.
example_zh: 市里今年给公共图书馆划拨了更多经费。

definition_en: the act of sharing something out, or the amount given to each part
example_en: Farmers argued over the allocation of water during the dry season.
example_zh: 旱季里农民们为水的分配争执不下。

definition_en: to mention something in an indirect way
example_en: The title of the song alludes to an old folk story.
example_zh: 这首歌的歌名暗指一个古老的民间故事。

definition_en: a repeated change from one thing to another and back again
example_en: The alternation of day and night controls many animals' behavior.
example_zh: 昼夜交替支配着许多动物的行为。

definition_en: existing in the surrounding area
example_en: Ambient noise from the street made it hard to hear the speaker.
example_zh: 街上的环境噪音让人很难听清讲话的人。

definition_en: having two opposite feelings about something at the same time
definition_zh: 心情矛盾的；态度摇摆的
example_en: She felt ambivalent about moving: excited, but also sad to leave.
example_zh: 对于搬家她心情矛盾：既兴奋，又舍不得离开。

definition_en: more than enough
example_en: There is ample evidence that exercise improves sleep.
example_zh: 有充分的证据表明运动能改善睡眠。

definition_en: to make something stronger, louder or greater
example_en: Social media can amplify a small rumor into a national story.
example_zh: 社交媒体能把一个小谣言放大成全国性的新闻。

definition_en: belonging to a different time; out of date for the period shown
definition_zh: 不合时代的；时代错置的
example_en: A wristwatch in a film about ancient Rome would be anachronistic.
example_zh: 在讲古罗马的电影里出现手表，就是时代错置。

definition_en: based on a comparison between two things that are alike in some way
example_en: Children often learn new ideas through analogical thinking.
example_zh: 孩子们常常通过类比的方式学习新概念。

definition_en: something that is similar to or matches something else
example_en: The town in the novel has a real-life analogue in the author's birthplace.
example_zh: 小说里的小镇在现实中有原型，就是作者的出生地。

definition_en: a comparison that explains one thing by showing how it is like another
example_en: The teacher used the analogy of a pump to explain how the heart works.
example_zh: 老师用水泵作类比来解释心脏是怎么工作的。

definition_en: belonging to or coming from family members who lived long ago
example_en: The family returned to their ancestral village every spring.
example_zh: 这家人每年春天都回到祖辈居住的村子。

definition_en: the family or group of living things that someone or something comes from
example_en: DNA tests can reveal surprising facts about a person's ancestry.
example_zh: DNA 检测能揭示一个人血统中出人意料的信息。

definition_en: based on personal stories or casual observation, not on careful study
definition_zh: 轶事的；基于个别见闻的
example_en: The evidence is only anecdotal, so researchers want a proper study.
example_zh: 这些证据只是零散的见闻，所以研究者希望做一项正式的研究。

definition_en: a short, interesting story about a real person or event
example_en: He began his speech with a funny anecdote about his first job.
example_zh: 他用第一份工作中的一件趣事作为演讲的开场。

definition_en: different from what is normal or expected
example_en: The anomalous result made the team repeat the experiment.
example_zh: 这个异常的结果让团队重做了实验。

definition_en: something that is different from what is normal or expected
example_en: A warm day in January is an anomaly in this region.
example_zh: 在这个地区，一月份出现暖和的天气属于反常。

definition_en: a collection of poems, stories or other writings by different authors
example_en: The poem appears in almost every anthology of American literature.
example_zh: 几乎每一本美国文学选集都收录了这首诗。

definition_en: a substance that helps protect cells from a certain kind of chemical damage
example_en: Blueberries are rich in antioxidants.
example_zh: 蓝莓富含抗氧化剂。

definition_en: the exact opposite of something
example_en: His calm manner is the antithesis of his brother's quick temper.
example_zh: 他沉稳的举止和他哥哥的急脾气正好相反。

definition_en: the set of equipment or supporting parts needed for a particular purpose
definition_zh: 器械；（成套的）配套材料；机构
example_en: The dictionary's apparatus includes notes, an index and maps.
example_zh: 这本词典的配套内容包括注释、索引和地图。

definition_en: almost correct or exact, but not completely so
example_en: Give me the approximate cost of the repairs.
example_zh: 告诉我维修的大概费用。

definition_en: close to a particular number or amount, but not exactly
example_en: The trip takes approximately two hours.
example_zh: 这趟路程大约需要两个小时。

definition_en: exactly suitable or right for the situation
example_en: "Quiet storm" is an apt description of her leadership style.
example_zh: 用“安静的风暴”来形容她的领导风格很贴切。

definition_en: living in or relating to water
example_en: Frogs spend the first part of their lives as aquatic animals.
example_zh: 青蛙生命的最初阶段是水生动物。

definition_en: containing water or dissolved in water
example_en: The chemist prepared an aqueous solution of salt.
example_zh: 化学家配制了盐的水溶液。

definition_en: (of land) suitable for growing crops
example_en: Only a small part of the mountainous country is arable.
example_zh: 这个多山的国家只有一小部分土地适合耕种。

definition_en: specialized or secret knowledge that only a few people understand
definition_zh: 只有少数人懂的专门知识；奥秘
example_en: The lawyer explained the arcana of tax law in plain words.
example_zh: 律师用通俗的话解释了税法里那些深奥难懂的内容。

definition_en: very old and no longer in common use
example_en: "Thou" is an archaic word for "you."
example_zh: “thou”是“you”的古语说法。

definition_en: the most typical example of a kind of person or thing; an original model
example_en: The wise old teacher is a familiar archetype in adventure stories.
example_zh: 睿智的老师是冒险故事里常见的人物原型。

definition_en: relating to a collection of historical records
example_en: The historian used archival letters to reconstruct the events.
example_zh: 历史学家利用档案里的信件还原了事件经过。

definition_en: having very little rain; very dry
example_en: Few crops can grow in such an arid region.
example_zh: 在这样干旱的地区很少有作物能生长。

definition_en: a large group or range of things
example_en: The store offers a wide array of fresh vegetables.
example_zh: 这家店提供种类繁多的新鲜蔬菜。

definition_en: done with great skill and cleverness
example_en: The chef's artful arrangement made the simple dish look special.
example_zh: 厨师巧妙的摆盘让这道简单的菜显得很特别。

definition_en: to express an idea clearly in words
example_en: She struggled to articulate why the painting moved her.
example_zh: 她很难说清这幅画为什么打动了她。

definition_en: an object made by people in the past, especially one of historical interest
definition_zh: （有历史价值的）人工制品；文物
example_en: The dig uncovered tools, pots and other artifacts.
example_zh: 这次发掘出土了工具、陶罐等文物。

definition_en: a clever trick or skillful design, often meant to deceive
example_en: The magician's show depended on artifice, not real magic.
example_zh: 魔术师的表演靠的是巧妙的手法，而不是真正的魔法。

definition_en: a strong hope or wish to achieve something
example_en: Her aspiration is to become the first doctor in her family.
example_zh: 她的志向是成为家里第一个医生。

definition_en: a collection of things found or gathered together
example_en: The cave held an assemblage of stone tools from different periods.
example_zh: 洞穴里有一批不同时期的石器。

definition_en: to state firmly that something is true
example_en: The author asserts that the old theory is wrong.
example_zh: 作者断言旧的理论是错的。

definition_en: a statement that something is true, made firmly
example_en: There is little evidence to support his assertion.
example_zh: 几乎没有证据支持他的说法。

definition_en: confident and direct in showing what you think or want
example_en: She stood in an assertive pose, with her hands on her hips.
example_zh: 她双手叉腰，站姿坚定自信。

definition_en: to reach or achieve something after effort
example_en: He attained the highest score in the school's history.
example_zh: 他取得了学校历史上的最高分。

definition_en: to make something weaker or thinner
example_en: Thick walls attenuate the noise from the street.
example_zh: 厚墙减弱了街上传来的噪音。

definition_en: to show or say that something is true
example_en: As any teacher will attest, no two classes are alike.
example_zh: 任何一位老师都可以证明，没有两个班是一样的。

definition_en: to say that something is caused by, or was made by, a particular thing or person
example_en: Scientists attribute the decline in bees to the loss of wildflowers.
example_zh: 科学家把蜜蜂数量的下降归因于野花的减少。

definition_en: to prove that something is real or genuine
example_en: Experts authenticated the letter by studying its ink and paper.
example_zh: 专家通过研究墨水和纸张鉴定这封信是真迹。

definition_en: relating to the author of a piece of writing
example_en: The stories were changed by editors without authorial approval.
example_zh: 这些故事未经作者同意就被编辑改动了。

definition_en: able to act or decide independently, without outside control
example_en: Autonomous learners set their own goals and check their own progress.
example_zh: 自主学习者会自己定目标、自己检查进度。

definition_en: a person or thing that gives extra help or support; supporting
example_en: The hospital has an auxiliary power supply for emergencies.
example_zh: 医院备有应急用的辅助电源。

definition_en: a strong feeling of not liking or not wanting something
example_en: Many investors have a strong aversion to risk.
example_zh: 许多投资者非常不愿意承担风险。

definition_en: relating to birds
example_en: Hawks and owls are avian predators.
example_zh: 鹰和猫头鹰是鸟类中的捕食者。

definition_en: a large room for formal dancing; (ballroom dance) formal dancing done by pairs
example_en: The waltz is a classic ballroom dance.
example_zh: 华尔兹是一种经典的交谊舞。

definition_en: a building or group of buildings where soldiers live
example_en: The soldiers returned to their barracks after training.
example_zh: 士兵们训练结束后回到营房。

definition_en: a large, low area of land, often one drained by a river
example_en: Millions of people live in the river basin.
example_zh: 有数百万人生活在这条河的流域内。

definition_en: coming or happening later than it should
example_en: He sent a belated birthday card a week after the party.
example_zh: 聚会过后一周，他才寄出一张迟到的生日贺卡。

definition_en: a person or group that gains from something
example_en: Small farms were the main beneficiaries of the new policy.
example_zh: 小农场是这项新政策的主要受益者。

definition_en: (old use) to cry over something; to mourn
example_en: In the old poem, the speaker beweeps his lonely state.
example_zh: 在那首古诗里，诗中人为自己的孤独处境悲泣。

definition_en: having two sides, or two matching halves
definition_zh: 两侧的；左右对称的；双边的
example_en: Humans have bilateral symmetry: the left side mirrors the right.
example_zh: 人体是左右对称的：左边和右边互为镜像。

definition_en: the gradual build-up of a chemical in the body of a living thing
example_en: Bioaccumulation of mercury makes some large fish unsafe to eat.
example_zh: 汞的生物累积使一些大型鱼类不宜食用。

definition_en: the variety of plants and animals living in a particular place
example_en: Rainforests are known for their rich biodiversity.
example_zh: 雨林以丰富的生物多样性著称。

definition_en: a detailed plan or drawing that shows how something will be built
example_en: The builders followed the architect's blueprint closely.
example_zh: 施工人员严格按照建筑师的图纸施工。

definition_en: to support or strengthen something
example_en: The new data bolster the argument that the climate is changing.
example_zh: 新的数据加强了气候正在变化这一论点。

definition_en: relating to the cold northern regions and their forests
definition_zh: 北方的；北方针叶林带的
example_en: Moose live in the boreal forests of Canada.
example_zh: 驼鹿生活在加拿大的北方森林里。

definition_en: relating to plants or the scientific study of plants
example_en: She drew botanical illustrations of rare flowers.
example_zh: 她为稀有花卉绘制植物图谱。

definition_en: a point where progress slows down because too much has to pass through
example_en: A shortage of drivers created a bottleneck in deliveries.
example_zh: 司机短缺造成了送货环节的瓶颈。

definition_en: a boxing or wrestling match; also a short period of activity or illness
example_en: The two wrestlers met in a five-minute bout.
example_zh: 两名摔跤手进行了一场五分钟的较量。

definition_en: a refusal to buy, use or take part in something as a protest
example_en: Shoppers organized a boycott of the company's products.
example_zh: 购物者发起了对这家公司产品的抵制。

definition_en: to quarrel or fight in a noisy way; a noisy fight
example_en: The two fans began to brawl outside the stadium.
example_zh: 两名球迷在体育场外大吵大闹起来。

definition_en: causing difficulty, worry or hard work
example_en: Small shops find the new paperwork burdensome.
example_zh: 小店觉得新增的文书工作是个负担。

definition_en: something that is produced during the making of something else
example_en: Heat is a by-product of running a computer.
example_zh: 热量是电脑运行时的副产物。

definition_en: because of; as a result of
example_en: She got the job by virtue of her long experience.
example_zh: 她凭借丰富的经验得到了这份工作。

definition_en: the rhythm and rise and fall of sounds or words
example_en: I recognized the gentle cadence of her voice at once.
example_zh: 我立刻听出了她那轻柔起伏的语调。

definition_en: an event that causes great harm or suffering
example_en: The flood was the worst calamity the town had ever faced.
example_zh: 那场洪水是这个小镇遭遇过的最严重的灾难。

definition_en: the process by which something becomes hard through a build-up of calcium
example_en: Corals build their skeletons through calcification.
example_zh: 珊瑚通过钙化作用形成骨骼。

definition_en: the part of a brake that presses against the wheel to stop it; also a tool for measuring thickness
example_en: The mechanic replaced the worn brake calipers.
example_zh: 修理工更换了磨损的刹车卡钳。

definition_en: a covering that spreads overhead, especially the top layer of leaves and branches in a forest
example_en: Monkeys travel through the forest canopy without touching the ground.
example_zh: 猴子在树冠间穿行，不用落地。

definition_en: to cook food slowly until its sugar turns brown and sweet
example_en: Caramelize the sugar in a pan before adding the cream.
example_zh: 先在锅里把糖熬成焦糖，再加入奶油。

definition_en: a person who makes maps
example_en: Early cartographers often left unexplored areas blank.
example_zh: 早期的制图师常常把未经勘探的地区留白。

definition_en: a person or thing that causes an important change to happen
definition_zh: 促成变化的因素；催化剂
example_en: The protest was a catalyst for changes in the law.
example_zh: 这次抗议促成了法律的修改。

definition_en: relating to how one thing makes another thing happen
example_en: The study found a causal link between smoking and lung disease.
example_zh: 这项研究发现吸烟和肺病之间存在因果关系。

definition_en: to stop happening or stop doing something
example_en: The factory ceased production in 1998.
example_zh: 这家工厂在 1998 年停产。

definition_en: relating to the sky or outer space
example_en: Stars, planets and moons are all celestial objects.
example_zh: 恒星、行星和卫星都是天体。

definition_en: an artist who makes objects from baked clay
example_en: The ceramist shaped the bowl by hand before firing it.
example_zh: 陶艺家先用手把碗塑好，再送去烧制。

definition_en: used in or relating to a formal traditional or religious event
example_en: The chief wore a ceremonial robe at the festival.
example_zh: 酋长在节庆上穿着礼仪用的长袍。

definition_en: the stopping of something
example_en: Both sides agreed to a cessation of fighting.
example_zh: 双方同意停止战斗。

definition_en: the use of strong contrasts between light and dark in a picture
example_en: The painter used chiaroscuro to make the face seem to glow.
example_zh: 画家运用明暗对比，让那张脸仿佛在发光。

definition_en: a written record of events in the order they happened; to record events this way
example_en: The book is a chronicle of life in a small fishing village.
example_zh: 这本书记述了一个小渔村的生活。

definition_en: arranged in the order in which events happened
example_en: The photos are displayed in chronological order.
example_zh: 这些照片按时间顺序陈列。

definition_en: (used before a date) about; approximately
example_en: The temple was built circa 800 CE.
example_zh: 这座神庙大约建于公元 800 年。

definition_en: to limit something within narrow boundaries
example_en: The king's power was circumscribed by the new laws.
example_zh: 国王的权力受到新法律的限制。

definition_en: relating to a town or city and the duties of the people who live there
example_en: Voting is an important civic duty.
example_zh: 投票是一项重要的公民义务。

definition_en: a large group of families who are related to each other
example_en: Everyone in the clan gathered for the wedding.
example_zh: 整个家族的人都来参加婚礼。

definition_en: a rounded stone, larger than a pebble
example_en: The beach was covered with smooth gray cobbles.
example_zh: 海滩上布满光滑的灰色卵石。

definition_en: relating to thinking, learning and understanding
example_en: Sleep is important for memory and other cognitive abilities.
example_zh: 睡眠对记忆和其他认知能力很重要。

definition_en: clear, logical and with all parts fitting together well
example_en: She gave a coherent account of what had happened.
example_zh: 她把事情的经过讲得条理清楚。

definition_en: the state in which parts fit together or stay united
example_en: Team sports can build cohesion among classmates.
example_zh: 集体运动可以增强同学之间的凝聚力。

definition_en: forming a united whole
definition_zh: 有凝聚力的；紧密结合的
example_en: The players work together as a cohesive group.
example_zh: 队员们配合默契，是一个团结的集体。

definition_en: a work made by combining many different pieces or materials
example_en: The students made a collage from old magazine pictures.
example_zh: 学生们用旧杂志上的图片做了一幅拼贴画。

definition_en: to hit something with force while moving
example_en: Two cars collided at the corner.
example_zh: 两辆车在拐角处相撞。

definition_en: a basic product that is bought and sold, such as grain or oil
example_en: Coffee is one of the most traded commodities in the world.
example_zh: 咖啡是世界上交易量最大的商品之一。

definition_en: similar enough to be compared
example_en: The two cities are comparable in size.
example_zh: 这两座城市规模相当。

definition_en: to force someone to do something (compelling, adj.: very convincing or interesting)
definition_zh: 迫使；（compelling）令人信服的、引人入胜的
example_en: Heavy snow compelled the school to close for a week.
example_zh: 大雪迫使学校停课一周。

definition_en: a collection of detailed information about a subject, usually in one book
example_en: The book is a compendium of traditional recipes.
example_zh: 这本书是一部传统菜谱大全。

definition_en: to make up for something bad or missing
example_en: Her speed compensates for her lack of height.
example_zh: 她的速度弥补了身高的不足。

definition_en: to go well with something and make it better or more complete
example_en: The sauce complements the flavor of the fish.
example_zh: 这种酱汁和鱼的味道相得益彰。

definition_en: the act of obeying a rule, law or request
example_en: The factory was inspected for compliance with safety rules.
example_zh: 工厂接受了是否遵守安全规定的检查。

definition_en: expressing praise; also, given free of charge
example_en: The reviews of her first film were highly complimentary.
example_zh: 对她第一部电影的评论赞誉有加。

definition_en: to consist of; to be made up of
example_en: The collection comprises more than 300 letters.
example_zh: 这批藏品包括三百多封信。

definition_en: to weaken or harm something; also, an agreement in which each side gives up something
example_en: A single error can compromise the results of the whole study.
example_zh: 一个错误就可能影响整项研究的结果。

definition_en: to admit that something is true, often unwillingly
example_en: He conceded that his opponent had made a good point.
example_zh: 他承认对手说得有道理。

definition_en: a clever or imaginative idea that a story, film or poem is built around
definition_zh: （作品的）奇特构思；巧妙的设定
example_en: The film's central conceit is that the hero relives the same day.
example_zh: 这部电影的核心设定是主人公反复过同一天。

definition_en: (of circles or rings) having the same center
example_en: A stone dropped in water produces concentric rings.
example_zh: 石头扔进水里会激起一圈圈同心的波纹。

definition_en: happening at the same time
example_en: The festival features several concurrent events.
example_zh: 这个节庆同时举办好几项活动。

definition_en: at the same time
example_en: The two studies were carried out concurrently.
example_zh: 两项研究是同时进行的。

definition_en: making it easy or likely for something to happen
example_en: A quiet room is conducive to study.
example_zh: 安静的房间有利于学习。

definition_en: a person you trust and tell your private thoughts to
definition_zh: 知己；可以吐露心事的人
example_en: Her sister was her closest confidant.
example_zh: 她姐姐是她最亲近的知己。

definition_en: to keep something within certain limits
example_en: Please confine your comments to the topic of today's meeting.
example_zh: 请把发言限定在今天会议的议题之内。

definition_en: to mix two different things together as if they were one
example_en: People often conflate weather with climate.
example_zh: 人们常把天气和气候混为一谈。

definition_en: the act of fitting or following a standard; also, the shape or structure of something
example_en: The job requires conformation to strict safety rules.
example_zh: 这份工作要求严格遵守安全规定。

definition_en: to come together in a group
example_en: Students congregate in the courtyard at lunchtime.
example_zh: 午饭时间学生们聚集在院子里。

definition_en: following one after another without a break
example_en: The team won five consecutive games.
example_zh: 这支队伍连胜五场。

definition_en: one after another without a break
example_en: The pages are numbered consecutively.
example_zh: 这些页是连续编号的。

definition_en: as a result
example_en: He missed the bus and consequently arrived late.
example_zh: 他没赶上公交车，所以迟到了。

definition_en: a group of organizations that work together on a project
example_en: A consortium of universities shared the cost of the telescope.
example_zh: 几所大学组成联合体，共同承担了望远镜的费用。

definition_en: belonging to the same species
example_en: The birds defend their nests against conspecific rivals.
example_zh: 这些鸟会保护自己的巢，抵御同种的竞争者。

definition_en: a group of stars that forms a pattern and has a name
example_en: Orion is one of the easiest constellations to find in the winter sky.
example_zh: 猎户座是冬季夜空中最容易找到的星座之一。

definition_en: a voter in the area that a politician represents; also, one of the parts of a whole
example_en: The senator met with her constituents to hear their concerns.
example_zh: 这位参议员会见了自己选区的选民，听取他们的意见。

definition_en: to form or make up something
example_en: Women constitute more than half of the company's staff.
example_zh: 女性占这家公司员工的一半以上。

definition_en: to limit what someone or something can do
example_en: The project was constrained by a very small budget.
example_zh: 这个项目受到预算太少的限制。

definition_en: something that limits what you can do
example_en: Time constraints forced us to cut the last scene.
example_zh: 由于时间限制，我们不得不删掉最后一场戏。

definition_en: to make something dirty or unsafe by adding a harmful substance
example_en: The river was contaminated by waste from the factory.
example_zh: 这条河被工厂排出的废料污染了。

definition_en: the presence of something harmful or unwanted that makes a thing impure
example_en: The lab wore gloves to prevent contamination of the samples.
example_zh: 实验室人员戴手套以防样品受到污染。

definition_en: to think about something deeply and for a long time
example_en: He sat by the window, contemplating his future.
example_zh: 他坐在窗边，思考着自己的未来。

definition_en: existing or happening in the same period of time
example_en: The diary gives a contemporaneous account of the war.
example_zh: 这本日记提供了对那场战争的同时期记录。

definition_en: during the same period of time
example_en: The two cities developed contemporaneously but independently.
example_zh: 这两座城市在同一时期各自独立发展起来。

definition_en: to argue or state firmly that something is true; (contend with) to have to deal with a difficulty
definition_zh: 主张；声称；（contend with）应对（困难）
example_en: Farmers are contending with the driest summer in decades.
example_zh: 农民们正在应对几十年来最干旱的夏天。

definition_en: depending on something else in order to happen
example_en: The trip is contingent on the weather.
example_zh: 这次出行要看天气情况而定。

definition_en: the state of continuing without a break; in film, keeping details the same from shot to shot
definition_zh: 连续性；（影视）镜头之间的连贯
example_en: A cup that changes hands between shots is a continuity error.
example_zh: 两个镜头之间杯子换了手，就是一处穿帮。

definition_en: to say or show the opposite of something
example_en: The new results contradict the earlier study.
example_zh: 新的结果与之前的研究相矛盾。

definition_en: a difference between two statements or facts that means both cannot be true
example_en: There is a contradiction between what he says and what he does.
example_zh: 他说的和做的自相矛盾。

definition_en: in the usual or traditional way
example_en: The poem is conventionally dated to the tenth century.
example_zh: 这首诗通常被认为写于十世纪。

definition_en: having knowledge or experience of something; familiar with it
example_en: New staff must be conversant with the safety rules.
example_zh: 新员工必须熟悉安全规定。

definition_en: in the opposite way; on the other hand
example_en: Rich soil helps plants grow; conversely, poor soil slows them down.
example_zh: 肥沃的土壤有助于植物生长；反过来，贫瘠的土壤会拖慢生长。

definition_en: to carry something from one place to another; to communicate an idea or feeling
example_en: Her letter conveys a deep sense of gratitude.
example_zh: 她的信传达出深深的感激之情。

definition_en: a business or organization owned and run together by its members
example_en: The farmers formed a cooperative to sell their milk.
example_zh: 农民们成立了一个合作社来销售牛奶。

definition_en: a complete collection of writings of a particular kind or by one author
example_en: The entire corpus of the poet's work fits in one volume.
example_zh: 这位诗人的全部作品一卷就能装下。

definition_en: to be closely connected, so that one thing changes as another does
example_en: Hours of study correlate strongly with test scores.
example_zh: 学习时长与考试成绩密切相关。

definition_en: a connection between two things in which one changes as the other does
example_en: Researchers found a correlation between sleep and memory.
example_zh: 研究人员发现睡眠和记忆之间存在关联。

definition_en: to match or be equal to something
example_en: Each number on the map corresponds to a building.
example_zh: 地图上的每个数字对应一栋建筑。

definition_en: a close similarity or connection between two things; also, letters exchanged
example_en: Readers noticed a correspondence between the hero's life and the author's.
example_zh: 读者注意到主人公的经历和作者本人的经历有相似之处。

definition_en: to give evidence that supports a statement or idea
example_en: A second witness corroborated her story.
example_zh: 第二位证人证实了她的说法。

definition_en: not easily damaged by rust or chemicals
example_en: Boats need corrosion-resistant metal parts.
example_zh: 船只需要耐腐蚀的金属零件。

definition_en: relating to the study of the universe as a whole
example_en: The telescope was built to answer cosmological questions.
example_zh: 建造这台望远镜是为了回答宇宙学问题。

definition_en: the universe
example_en: Humans have always wondered about their place in the cosmos.
example_zh: 人类一直想知道自己在宇宙中的位置。

definition_en: the quality of being very expensive
example_en: The costliness of the palace shocked ordinary citizens.
example_zh: 这座宫殿的豪奢让普通市民震惊。

definition_en: an idea about what would have happened if events had been different
example_en: "What if the war had never begun?" is a famous counterfactual.
example_zh: “如果那场战争从未爆发会怎样？”是一个著名的反事实设想。

definition_en: a person or thing with the same role as another in a different place or group
example_en: The mayor met her counterpart from the neighboring city.
example_zh: 市长会见了邻市的市长。

definition_en: having the opposite effect to the one you wanted
example_en: Studying all night before a test can be counterproductive.
example_zh: 考前通宵学习可能适得其反。

definition_en: relating to the court of a king or queen; very polite and formal
example_en: Dancing was a popular courtly pastime.
example_zh: 跳舞是很受欢迎的宫廷消遣。

definition_en: an activity that needs special skill; (v.) to make or write something with skill and care
definition_zh: 技艺；手艺；精心制作（撰写）
example_en: She spent years learning the craft of storytelling.
example_zh: 她花了多年时间学习讲故事的技艺。

definition_en: a standard by which something is judged (plural: criteria)
example_en: Price was the main criterion in choosing a hotel.
example_zh: 价格是选酒店的主要标准。

definition_en: a detailed judgment of something's strengths and weaknesses; to examine and judge
example_en: The essay offers a sharp critique of modern advertising.
example_zh: 这篇文章对现代广告提出了尖锐的批评。

definition_en: simple and not skillfully made; rough
example_en: They built a crude shelter from branches.
example_zh: 他们用树枝搭了一个简陋的棚子。

definition_en: the hard outer layer of something, such as bread or fried food
example_en: The bread has a thick golden crust.
example_zh: 这种面包有一层厚厚的金黄色外皮。

definition_en: having a hidden meaning that is hard to understand
example_en: He left a cryptic note that nobody could explain.
example_zh: 他留下一张谁也看不懂的神秘字条。

definition_en: a signal that tells someone or something to act
example_en: Falling temperatures are a cue for birds to fly south.
example_zh: 气温下降是鸟类南飞的信号。

definition_en: to grow plants or crops; to try to develop something
example_en: Farmers in the valley cultivate rice and beans.
example_zh: 山谷里的农民种植水稻和豆类。

definition_en: the growing of plants and crops
example_en: The cultivation of tea began in China.
example_zh: 茶的种植始于中国。

definition_en: increasing as more and more is added over time
example_en: The cumulative effect of small savings can be large.
example_zh: 小额储蓄累积起来的效果可能很可观。

definition_en: a person in charge of a museum's collection or of an exhibition
example_en: The curator chose forty photographs for the show.
example_zh: 策展人为这次展览挑选了四十幅照片。

definition_en: relating to the work of selecting and caring for objects in a museum
example_en: The museum's curatorial team planned the new exhibit.
example_zh: 博物馆的策展团队策划了这个新展览。

definition_en: the state of being curved, or how much something curves
example_en: From space you can clearly see the curvature of Earth.
example_zh: 从太空可以清楚地看到地球的弧度。

definition_en: the time of day when light first appears; the beginning of something
example_en: The fishermen leave the harbor at dawn.
example_zh: 渔民们在黎明时分离开港口。

definition_en: a lack of something; too little of it
example_en: There is a dearth of good housing in the city.
example_zh: 这座城市缺少好的住房。

definition_en: broken pieces left after something is destroyed or used
example_en: After the storm, the streets were full of debris.
example_zh: 暴风雨过后，街上满是残枝碎物。

definition_en: the first public appearance; to appear or be shown for the first time
example_en: The band's debut album sold a million copies.
example_zh: 这支乐队的首张专辑卖出了一百万张。

definition_en: to make someone believe something that is not true
example_en: Some insects deceive predators by looking like leaves.
example_zh: 有些昆虫靠长得像树叶来蒙骗捕食者。

definition_en: to slow down
example_en: The train decelerated as it approached the station.
example_zh: 火车驶近车站时减速了。

definition_en: the act of making someone believe something untrue
example_en: The plan depended on deception rather than force.
example_zh: 这个计划靠的是欺骗而不是武力。

definition_en: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from the facts you know
example_en: From the wet floor, she deduced that someone had just come in.
example_zh: 看到地板是湿的，她推断刚刚有人进来过。

definition_en: to consider or judge something in a particular way
example_en: The bridge was deemed unsafe and closed.
example_zh: 这座桥被认定不安全，已经封闭。

definition_en: not working properly; having a fault
example_en: The store replaced the defective phone for free.
example_zh: 商店免费更换了那部有毛病的手机。

definition_en: to delay something until a later time
example_en: She deferred her studies for a year to travel.
example_zh: 她推迟了一年学业去旅行。

definition_en: polite respect, shown by accepting another person's wishes or opinions
example_en: The students listened in deference to the old teacher.
example_zh: 出于对老教师的尊重，学生们静静地听着。

definition_en: final and certain; not able to be questioned
example_en: There is no definitive answer to this question yet.
example_zh: 这个问题目前还没有确定的答案。

definition_en: to refuse to obey; to resist
example_en: The workers defied the order and stayed outside.
example_zh: 工人们不服从命令，留在了外面。

definition_en: the process of something becoming worse or damaged
example_en: Soil degradation threatens food production.
example_zh: 土壤退化威胁着粮食生产。

definition_en: to make something worse in quality; to damage
example_en: Pollution has degraded the water in the lake.
example_zh: 污染使湖水水质变差了。

definition_en: done on purpose, not by accident
example_en: The mistake was accidental, not deliberate.
example_zh: 这个错误是无意的，不是故意的。

definition_en: on purpose
example_en: She deliberately left the window open.
example_zh: 她故意把窗户开着。

definition_en: involving careful thought and discussion
example_en: A jury's deliberative process can take several days.
example_zh: 陪审团的审议过程可能要花好几天。

definition_en: to mark or fix the limits of something
example_en: A fence delimits the school's property.
example_zh: 一道围栏划出了学校的范围。

definition_en: the way a person behaves and appears to others
example_en: Her calm demeanor reassured the passengers.
example_zh: 她镇定的神态让乘客们安下心来。

definition_en: a scientist who studies tree rings to date past events
example_en: A dendrochronologist can tell how old a tree is from its rings.
example_zh: 树木年轮学家能根据年轮判断一棵树的年龄。

definition_en: with many people or things close together
example_en: The coast is the most densely populated part of the country.
example_zh: 沿海是这个国家人口最密集的地区。

definition_en: to show or describe something in a picture or in words
example_en: The mural depicts daily life in the village.
example_zh: 这幅壁画描绘了村里的日常生活。

definition_en: to put something into use for a particular purpose
example_en: The writer deploys humor to make a serious point.
example_zh: 作者运用幽默来表达一个严肃的观点。

definition_en: to put or leave something in a place, often in layers; an amount left there
definition_zh: 沉积；放置；沉积物；存放物
example_en: The river deposits mud along its banks every spring.
example_zh: 这条河每年春天都在两岸沉积淤泥。

definition_en: the process of laying down material in layers
example_en: The 3D printer builds objects by the deposition of thin layers of plastic.
example_zh: 这台 3D 打印机靠一层层堆积薄薄的塑料来制作物体。

definition_en: to laugh at or speak of something as worthless
example_en: Critics derided the painting when it was first shown.
example_zh: 这幅画首次展出时遭到评论家的嘲笑。

definition_en: copied from something else and not original; a thing based on another
example_en: The film was criticized as derivative of earlier thrillers.
example_zh: 这部电影被批评为对早期惊悚片的模仿。

definition_en: to get something from a source; to come from
example_en: The word "piano" derives from Italian.
example_zh: “piano”一词源自意大利语。

definition_en: a person's or animal's family origin; also, a movement downward
example_en: Many people in the town are of Irish descent.
example_zh: 镇上许多人有爱尔兰血统。

definition_en: to officially choose or name something for a particular purpose
example_en: The area was designated a national park in 1990.
example_zh: 这个地区在 1990 年被划为国家公园。

definition_en: an official name, title or description
example_en: The building received the designation "historic landmark."
example_zh: 这座建筑获得了“历史地标”的称号。

definition_en: to stop someone from doing something by making it seem difficult or dangerous
example_en: Bright colors deter predators from eating the frog.
example_zh: 鲜艳的颜色让捕食者不敢吃这种青蛙。

definition_en: to do something different from what is usual or expected
example_en: The pilot deviated from the planned route to avoid a storm.
example_zh: 飞行员偏离了原定航线以避开风暴。

definition_en: a difference from what is usual or expected
example_en: Any deviation from the recipe may spoil the cake.
example_zh: 稍微偏离配方都可能把蛋糕做坏。

definition_en: to invent a plan, system or method
example_en: The students devised a new way to recycle plastic.
example_zh: 学生们想出了一种回收塑料的新办法。

definition_en: to find out what illness or problem someone or something has
example_en: The doctor diagnosed the problem after a few tests.
example_zh: 医生做了几项检查后诊断出了问题。

definition_en: the length of a straight line across a circle through its center
example_en: The table is one meter in diameter.
example_zh: 这张桌子直径一米。

definition_en: a difference in amount between two things
example_en: The price differential between the two brands is small.
example_zh: 这两个品牌之间的价格差很小。

definition_en: the act of separating things into different kinds; becoming different
example_en: The model depends on the differentiation of plants into three groups.
example_zh: 这个模型依赖于把植物划分为三类。

definition_en: the spreading of something over a wide area or among many people
example_en: The internet sped up the diffusion of new ideas.
example_zh: 互联网加快了新思想的传播。

definition_en: calm, serious and deserving respect
example_en: She gave a dignified reply to the rude question.
example_zh: 面对无礼的提问，她回答得很得体。

definition_en: to move away from the main subject in speech or writing
example_en: The speaker digressed from his topic to tell a joke.
example_zh: 演讲者岔开话题讲了个笑话。

definition_en: not bright; hard to see
example_en: The stars looked dim through the city haze.
example_zh: 透过城市的雾霾，星星显得很暗淡。

definition_en: to become or make something smaller, weaker or less important
example_en: The medicine diminished the pain within an hour.
example_zh: 药物在一小时内减轻了疼痛。

definition_en: a reduction in size, amount or importance
example_en: The report noted a diminution in bird numbers.
example_zh: 报告指出鸟类数量有所减少。

definition_en: having breaks or gaps; not continuous
example_en: The mountain range is discontinuous, broken by wide valleys.
example_zh: 这条山脉并不连续，被宽阔的山谷隔断。

definition_en: serious discussion or writing about a subject
example_en: Climate change is now central to political discourse.
example_zh: 气候变化如今是政治讨论的核心议题。

definition_en: a difference between two things that should be the same
example_en: There was a discrepancy between the two reports of the accident.
example_zh: 关于这起事故的两份报告有出入。

definition_en: (of writing) explaining and arguing in a direct way, moving from point to point
example_en: The book mixes poetry with long discursive passages.
example_zh: 这本书把诗歌和大段的论述文字穿插在一起。

definition_en: a gap or lack of connection between two things
example_en: The film shows the disjuncture between his dreams and his real life.
example_zh: 这部电影展现了他的梦想与现实生活之间的落差。

definition_en: not faithful to a person, group or country
example_en: The king punished those he believed were disloyal.
example_zh: 国王惩罚了那些他认为不忠的人。

definition_en: showing that you think something is not worth attention
example_en: He gave a dismissive wave and walked away.
example_zh: 他不屑地摆了摆手就走开了。

definition_en: very different from each other
example_en: The band blends disparate styles such as jazz and folk.
example_zh: 这支乐队融合了爵士、民谣等迥然不同的风格。

definition_en: a noticeable and often unfair difference
example_en: There is a wide disparity in income between the two regions.
example_zh: 这两个地区的收入差距很大。

definition_en: the spreading of people, animals or seeds over a wide area
example_en: Wind plays a major role in the dispersal of seeds.
example_zh: 风在种子的传播中起着重要作用。

definition_en: to spread or scatter over a wide area
example_en: Birds disperse seeds by eating fruit and flying away.
example_zh: 鸟类吃下果实后飞走，从而传播种子。

definition_en: an animal or thing that spreads seeds or other things over an area
definition_zh: 传播者（尤指传播种子的动物）
example_en: Bats are important seed dispersers in tropical forests.
example_zh: 蝙蝠是热带森林中重要的种子传播者。

definition_en: the spreading of things over a wide area
example_en: The map shows the dispersion of the species across the island.
example_zh: 这张地图显示了该物种在岛上的分布扩散情况。

definition_en: to move something from its usual place; to shift something onto others
example_en: The company displaced the cost of repairs onto its customers.
example_zh: 这家公司把维修成本转嫁给了顾客。

definition_en: a person's usual mood or character
example_en: He has a cheerful disposition and rarely complains.
example_zh: 他性格开朗，很少抱怨。

definition_en: to show that something is false
example_en: The experiment disproved the old theory.
example_zh: 这个实验推翻了旧的理论。

definition_en: to pay no attention to something; to ignore
example_en: The driver disregarded the warning signs.
example_zh: 司机无视了警示牌。

definition_en: to spread information or ideas to many people
example_en: The findings were disseminated through newspapers and radio.
example_zh: 这些发现通过报纸和广播传播开来。

definition_en: to mix into a liquid and disappear; to fade away
example_en: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water.
example_zh: 糖在热水里溶解得更快。

definition_en: a clear difference between similar things
example_en: The law makes a distinction between adults and children.
example_zh: 法律对成年人和儿童作了区分。

definition_en: having a special quality that makes something easy to recognize
example_en: The bird has a distinctive red patch on its head.
example_zh: 这种鸟头上有一块独特的红斑。

definition_en: to recognize or show the difference between things; to make something stand out as different
example_en: Its red tail distinguishes this bird from similar ones.
example_zh: 红色的尾巴使这种鸟有别于相似的鸟。

definition_en: the feeling that you cannot trust someone or something
example_en: There is deep distrust between the two leaders.
example_zh: 两位领导人之间互不信任。

definition_en: something that interrupts a calm or normal condition
example_en: Even a small disturbance can wake the sleeping birds.
example_zh: 哪怕一点小动静也会惊醒睡着的鸟。

definition_en: the state of no longer being used
example_en: The old canal fell into disuse after the railway was built.
example_zh: 铁路修好之后，旧运河就废弃了。

definition_en: having two syllables
example_en: "Table" and "window" are disyllabic words.
example_zh: “table”和“window”都是双音节词。

definition_en: to become different; to separate and go in different directions
example_en: Their opinions diverge on how to spend the money.
example_zh: 在怎么花这笔钱的问题上，他们意见不一。

definition_en: different from each other; moving apart
example_en: The two witnesses gave divergent accounts.
example_zh: 两名证人的说法不一致。

definition_en: the act of adding variety, for example by growing more kinds of crops
example_en: Crop diversification protects farmers when one harvest fails.
example_zh: 作物多样化能在某一种作物歉收时保护农民。

definition_en: to turn something away from its course or from its purpose
example_en: The noise diverted my attention from the book.
example_zh: 噪音把我的注意力从书上引开了。

definition_en: a principle or set of beliefs that is taught and accepted
example_en: The court rejected the old legal doctrine.
example_zh: 法院否定了那条旧的法律原则。

definition_en: to change wild plants or animals so that people can grow or keep them
example_en: Humans domesticated wheat about ten thousand years ago.
example_zh: 人类大约在一万年前驯化了小麦。

definition_en: the process of changing wild plants or animals for human use
example_en: The domestication of the horse changed travel forever.
example_zh: 马的驯化永远改变了人们的出行方式。

definition_en: a period when business activity or the economy gets worse
example_en: Many shops closed during the economic downturn.
example_zh: 经济低迷期间许多商店关门了。

definition_en: to hang or bend downward
example_en: The flowers drooped in the afternoon heat.
example_zh: 花在午后的热气中耷拉下来。

definition_en: a long period with little or no rain
example_en: The drought destroyed most of the corn crop.
example_zh: 旱灾毁掉了大部分玉米收成。

definition_en: hard, boring work
definition_zh: 苦差事；单调乏味的工作
example_en: Machines freed people from much household drudgery.
example_zh: 机器把人们从许多繁重乏味的家务中解放出来。

definition_en: the quality of lasting a long time without damage
example_en: These boots are known for their durability.
example_zh: 这种靴子以耐穿著称。

definition_en: strong and able to last a long time
example_en: Stone is a durable building material.
example_zh: 石头是一种耐用的建筑材料。

definition_en: the length of time that something lasts
example_en: Phones must be switched off for the duration of the flight.
example_zh: 飞行全程必须关闭手机。

definition_en: energy, activity and a readiness for change
example_en: The city is known for its economic dynamism.
example_zh: 这座城市以经济活力著称。

definition_en: the quality of being serious and sincere
example_en: She spoke with such earnestness that everyone believed her.
example_zh: 她说得那么恳切，大家都相信了她。

definition_en: a long, thin worm that lives in soil
example_en: Earthworms help keep garden soil healthy.
example_zh: 蚯蚓有助于保持花园土壤的健康。

definition_en: a time when the sun or moon is hidden by another body; to make something seem less important
example_en: Her success eclipsed that of her older brother.
example_zh: 她的成就使她哥哥相形见绌。

definition_en: a person whose job is to teach or to plan how people are taught
example_en: The educator designed a new reading program.
example_zh: 这位教育工作者设计了一套新的阅读课程。

definition_en: to push or throw something out with force
example_en: The volcano ejected ash high into the air.
example_zh: 火山把火山灰喷向高空。

definition_en: with a lot of careful detail or decoration
example_en: The cake was elaborately decorated with sugar flowers.
example_zh: 蛋糕上用糖花作了精致繁复的装饰。

definition_en: to raise something to a higher level or position
example_en: The award elevated her to national fame.
example_zh: 这个奖项让她享誉全国。

definition_en: to draw out a reaction, answer or feeling
example_en: The joke elicited laughter from the whole class.
example_zh: 这个笑话引得全班大笑。

definition_en: the process of becoming longer
example_en: Warm weather causes rapid elongation of the plant's stems.
example_zh: 温暖的天气使这种植物的茎迅速伸长。

definition_en: hard to find, catch or achieve
definition_zh: 难以找到的；难以实现的
example_en: A cure for the disease has remained elusive.
example_zh: 这种病的治疗方法至今仍未找到。

definition_en: to fix something firmly inside something else
example_en: The show has advertisements embedded in the story.
example_zh: 这个节目把广告嵌进了剧情里。

definition_en: decorative patterns sewn onto cloth
example_en: My grandmother taught me traditional embroidery.
example_zh: 祖母教我传统刺绣。

definition_en: the process of appearing or coming into existence
example_en: The emergence of the internet changed how people shop.
example_zh: 互联网的出现改变了人们的购物方式。

definition_en: to leave your own country or region to live in another
example_en: His grandparents emigrated from Italy in 1920.
example_zh: 他的祖父母在 1920 年从意大利移居国外。

definition_en: the sending out of light, gas or heat; the amount sent out
example_en: The city wants to cut carbon emissions by half.
example_zh: 这座城市想把碳排放量减半。

definition_en: to send out light, heat, sound or gas
example_en: The lamp emits a soft yellow light.
example_zh: 这盏灯发出柔和的黄光。

definition_en: the process of gaining the power and confidence to control your own life
example_en: Education is a path to empowerment for many girls.
example_zh: 对许多女孩来说，教育是获得自主能力的途径。

definition_en: a substance that helps two liquids such as oil and water stay mixed
example_en: Egg yolk works as an emulsifier in mayonnaise.
example_zh: 蛋黄在蛋黄酱里起乳化剂的作用。

definition_en: a mixture of two liquids that do not normally mix, such as oil and water
example_en: Milk is an emulsion of fat in water.
example_zh: 牛奶是脂肪分散在水中形成的乳浊液。

definition_en: to make something happen or put it into effect, especially a law or change
example_en: The government enacted new rules to protect forests.
example_zh: 政府颁布了保护森林的新规定。

definition_en: the act of making something into law or putting it into effect
example_en: Problems appeared two years after the law's enactment.
example_zh: 这部法律颁布两年后，问题开始显现。

definition_en: (of painting) done with colors mixed into hot wax
example_en: Encaustic painting requires the artist to work with melted wax.
example_zh: 热蜡画要求画家用融化的蜡来作画。

definition_en: an area surrounded by a wall or fence
example_en: The fish were kept in a stone enclosure near the shore.
example_zh: 鱼被养在岸边一个用石头围成的池子里。

definition_en: to include a wide range of things
example_en: The course encompasses art, music and literature.
example_zh: 这门课程涵盖美术、音乐和文学。

definition_en: a public statement of support or approval
example_en: The candidate won the endorsement of several newspapers.
example_zh: 这位候选人得到了几家报纸的公开支持。

definition_en: to continue to exist for a long time; to suffer something patiently (enduring, adj.: long-lasting)
example_en: The friendship endured for more than fifty years.
example_zh: 这段友谊持续了五十多年。

definition_en: the act of making people obey a law or rule
example_en: Strict enforcement of the rule reduced accidents.
example_zh: 严格执行这条规定之后，事故减少了。

definition_en: to cause a feeling or situation to exist
example_en: The coach's honesty engendered trust among the players.
example_zh: 教练的坦诚赢得了队员们的信任。

definition_en: to improve something or make it stronger
example_en: Good lighting enhances the beauty of the room.
example_zh: 好的灯光让房间显得更美。

definition_en: mysterious and difficult to understand
example_en: The portrait is famous for its enigmatic smile.
example_zh: 这幅肖像以神秘的微笑闻名。

definition_en: to get someone's help or support; to sign someone up to take part
example_en: The researchers enlisted two hundred volunteers for the study.
example_zh: 研究人员为这项研究招募了两百名志愿者。

definition_en: a strong feeling of hatred between people
example_en: Years of enmity divided the two families.
example_zh: 多年的仇怨使两家人势同水火。

definition_en: to involve something as a necessary part or result
example_en: The job entails a lot of travel.
example_zh: 这份工作需要经常出差。

definition_en: a person who is very interested in a particular activity or subject
example_en: Bird enthusiasts gather here every spring.
example_zh: 每年春天观鸟爱好者都聚集在这里。

definition_en: something that exists as a separate, single thing
example_en: The two companies merged into a single entity.
example_zh: 两家公司合并成了一个实体。

definition_en: firmly established and very hard to change
example_en: The custom is deeply entrenched in local culture.
example_zh: 这个习俗在当地文化中根深蒂固。

definition_en: a person who starts a business and takes financial risks to do so
example_en: The young entrepreneur opened her first bakery at nineteen.
example_zh: 这位年轻的创业者十九岁就开了第一家面包店。

definition_en: to imagine something as a future or possible situation
example_en: She envisions a city with no cars in its center.
example_zh: 她设想的是一座市中心没有汽车的城市。

definition_en: told or happening in separate parts or episodes
definition_zh: 分集的；由一个个片段组成的
example_en: The novel has an episodic structure, like a TV series.
example_zh: 这部小说的结构是一段一段的，像电视连续剧。

definition_en: written in the form of letters
example_en: An epistolary novel tells its story through letters.
example_zh: 书信体小说通过一封封信来讲故事。

definition_en: a long period of time in history or in Earth's past
example_en: The invention of printing began a new epoch in learning.
example_zh: 印刷术的发明开启了学术的新时代。

definition_en: the imaginary line around the middle of Earth, halfway between the poles
example_en: Countries near the equator are warm all year.
example_zh: 赤道附近的国家全年温暖。

definition_en: the value that something such as a company or brand holds; also, fairness
example_en: A trusted name adds to a brand's equity.
example_zh: 值得信赖的名声会提升品牌价值。

definition_en: the act of removing or wiping something out completely
example_en: The mural's erasure angered people in the neighborhood.
example_zh: 壁画被抹掉，激怒了街区的居民。

definition_en: the gradual wearing away of soil or rock by wind or water
example_en: Tree roots help prevent soil erosion.
example_zh: 树根有助于防止水土流失。

definition_en: to deliberately avoid or give up something
example_en: The designer eschews bright colors in favor of gray and white.
example_zh: 这位设计师不用鲜艳的颜色，而偏爱灰色和白色。

definition_en: the most basic and important quality of something
example_en: The essence of his argument is that prices are too high.
example_zh: 他论点的核心是价格太高。

definition_en: relating to the study of people's cultures by observing their daily lives
definition_zh: 民族志的；实地观察人群文化的
example_en: The researcher spent a year doing ethnographic fieldwork in the village.
example_zh: 这位研究者在村里做了一年的民族志田野调查。

definition_en: a living thing whose cells have a nucleus, such as an animal, plant or fungus
example_en: Humans, trees and mushrooms are all eukaryotes.
example_zh: 人、树和蘑菇都是真核生物。

definition_en: to escape from or avoid something
example_en: The fox evaded the hunters by crossing the river.
example_zh: 狐狸过了河，躲开了猎人。

definition_en: to change from a liquid into a gas
example_en: The puddles evaporated in the hot sun.
example_zh: 水坑在烈日下蒸发了。

definition_en: to make something seem larger, better or worse than it really is
example_en: He tends to exaggerate the size of the fish he catches.
example_zh: 他喜欢夸大自己钓到的鱼有多大。

definition_en: to dig in the ground, especially to find ancient objects
example_en: Archaeologists excavated a Roman villa near the river.
example_zh: 考古学家在河边发掘出一座罗马别墅。

definition_en: much more than is reasonable or necessary
example_en: Excessive noise can damage your hearing.
example_zh: 过大的噪音会损害听力。

definition_en: to a degree that is too great
example_en: The essay focuses excessively on minor details.
example_zh: 这篇文章过分关注细枝末节。

definition_en: to remove something by cutting it out
example_en: The editor excised two chapters from the book.
example_zh: 编辑从书中删去了两章。

definition_en: the act of leaving something or someone out
example_en: He studied physics to the exclusion of everything else.
example_zh: 他只学物理，别的一概不顾。

definition_en: limited to only one thing or group; not shared
example_en: The report gives exclusive attention to costs.
example_zh: 这份报告只关注成本。

definition_en: only; and nothing or no one else
example_en: The shop sells exclusively local products.
example_zh: 这家店只卖本地产品。

definition_en: a typical or very good example of something
example_en: The bridge is an exemplar of modern engineering.
example_zh: 这座桥是现代工程的典范。

definition_en: to be a typical example of something
example_en: Her career exemplifies the value of hard work.
example_zh: 她的职业生涯是勤奋价值的典型例证。

definition_en: a planet that orbits a star outside our solar system
example_en: Astronomers have found thousands of exoplanets.
example_zh: 天文学家已经发现了数千颗系外行星。

definition_en: a wide, open area of land, sea or sky
example_en: The boat crossed a great expanse of open water.
example_zh: 小船驶过一大片开阔的水面。

definition_en: an organized journey for a purpose such as research or exploration
example_en: The team set out on an expedition to the Arctic.
example_zh: 团队出发前往北极考察。

definition_en: the act of spending money, or the amount spent
example_en: Public expenditure on health rose last year.
example_zh: 去年公共卫生支出有所增加。

definition_en: special skill or knowledge in a particular subject
example_en: The project needs someone with legal expertise.
example_zh: 这个项目需要有法律专长的人。

definition_en: the state of being in contact with something, often something harmful
example_en: Long exposure to loud music can harm hearing.
example_zh: 长时间接触大音量音乐会损伤听力。

definition_en: showing thoughts and feelings clearly
example_en: Her face is very expressive when she tells a story.
example_zh: 她讲故事时表情非常丰富。

definition_en: extremely beautiful and delicately made
example_en: The ring was set with an exquisite blue stone.
example_zh: 戒指上镶着一颗精美的蓝宝石。

definition_en: spoken or done without preparation
example_en: She gave an extemporaneous speech that moved the audience.
example_zh: 她即兴发表了一段演讲，打动了听众。

definition_en: large in amount or covering a wide area
example_en: The library has an extensive collection of maps.
example_zh: 这家图书馆收藏了大量地图。

definition_en: (of a type of animal or plant) no longer existing
example_en: Dinosaurs became extinct millions of years ago.
example_zh: 恐龙在数千万年前灭绝了。

definition_en: the state in which a kind of animal or plant no longer exists
example_en: The tiger is in danger of extinction.
example_zh: 老虎有灭绝的危险。

definition_en: to push a soft material out through a small opening to shape it
example_en: The machine extrudes dough to form long noodles.
example_zh: 机器把面团挤出来做成长面条。

definition_en: the process of pushing material out through an opening to shape it
example_en: Plastic pipes are made by extrusion.
example_zh: 塑料管是用挤出工艺制成的。

definition_en: full of energy, excitement and happiness
definition_zh: 热情洋溢的；兴高采烈的
example_en: The exuberant crowd sang all the way home.
example_zh: 兴高采烈的人群一路唱着歌回家。

definition_en: to make an action or process easier
example_en: The new bridge facilitates trade between the two towns.
example_zh: 这座新桥方便了两个镇之间的贸易。

definition_en: to help someone learn about or get used to something
example_en: The first lesson familiarizes students with the lab equipment.
example_zh: 第一节课让学生熟悉实验器材。

definition_en: strange and imaginative, as if from a fantasy
example_en: The book is full of fantastical creatures such as dragons.
example_zh: 这本书里满是龙之类的奇幻生物。

definition_en: relating to the animals of a particular region or period
example_en: Faunal remains at the site include deer and fish bones.
example_zh: 遗址中的动物遗存包括鹿骨和鱼骨。

definition_en: an impressive achievement that needs skill, strength or courage
example_en: Climbing the mountain in winter was a remarkable feat.
example_zh: 冬天登上那座山是了不起的壮举。

definition_en: an award or position that gives money to support someone's work or study
definition_zh: （资助性质的）奖金；研究员职位
example_en: She won a fellowship to study folk music.
example_zh: 她获得了一笔研究民间音乐的奖金。

definition_en: (of an animal) living wild after having been kept by people
definition_zh: 野化的；（家养动物）变野的
example_en: Feral cats live in the old factory.
example_zh: 旧工厂里住着野化的猫。

definition_en: able to produce many crops or new ideas; rich
example_en: The river valley has fertile soil.
example_zh: 河谷的土壤很肥沃。

definition_en: the quality of staying true or faithful to something
example_en: The film was praised for its fidelity to the novel.
example_zh: 这部电影因忠实于原著而受到好评。

definition_en: using words in an imaginative, not literal, way
example_en: "Time is a river" is a figurative expression.
example_zh: “时间是一条河”是比喻的说法。

definition_en: a very thin thread or wire
example_en: The filament in an old light bulb glows when heated.
example_zh: 旧式灯泡里的灯丝受热就会发光。

definition_en: a fault or weakness (flawed, adj.: having a fault)
example_en: The plan has one serious flaw: it costs too much.
example_zh: 这个计划有一个严重的缺陷：花费太高。

definition_en: a group of birds or sheep; to gather or move in a large group
example_en: A flock of geese flew over the lake.
example_zh: 一群大雁飞过湖面。

definition_en: to grow or develop well; (n.) a decorative detail
definition_zh: 繁荣；茂盛；装饰性的细节
example_en: The town flourished after the railway arrived.
example_zh: 铁路通了以后，这个小镇繁荣起来。

definition_en: a change in level or amount that goes up and down
example_en: Farmers worry about fluctuations in grain prices.
example_zh: 农民担心粮价的波动。

definition_en: light given off by a substance after it absorbs light or other energy
example_en: Under the lamp, the mineral showed a green fluorescence.
example_zh: 在灯下，这种矿物发出绿色荧光。

definition_en: a flow of something; also, a state of continuous change
example_en: Scientists measured the flux of heat from the ground.
example_zh: 科学家测量了地面散发的热流量。

definition_en: food for farm animals; also, material that is useful for a purpose
example_en: The scandal provided fodder for comedians.
example_zh: 这桩丑闻给喜剧演员提供了素材。

definition_en: a person or thing that contrasts with another and so makes its qualities clearer
example_en: The quiet sister serves as a foil to the talkative hero.
example_zh: 安静的妹妹正好衬托出健谈的主人公。

definition_en: a traditional story passed down by word of mouth
example_en: The folktale explains how the fox got its red coat.
example_zh: 这个民间故事讲的是狐狸怎么有了一身红毛。

definition_en: to search for food; (n.) plants eaten by farm animals
example_en: Bears forage for berries in late summer.
example_zh: 夏末时熊会四处找浆果吃。

definition_en: strong and confident; having a powerful effect
example_en: She made a forceful argument for change.
example_zh: 她有力地论证了变革的必要。

definition_en: a statement of what is expected to happen; to predict
example_en: The weather forecast says it will snow tomorrow.
example_zh: 天气预报说明天会下雪。

definition_en: a worker who leads and directs a group of other workers
example_en: The foreperson checked every worker's safety gear.
example_zh: 领班检查了每个工人的安全装备。

definition_en: to create something strong and lasting through effort
example_en: The two schools forged a close partnership.
example_zh: 这两所学校建立了紧密的合作关系。

definition_en: to develop or express an idea or plan carefully
example_en: The team formulated a plan to cut costs.
example_zh: 团队制定了一个削减成本的计划。

definition_en: a mixture prepared in a particular way; the way something is expressed
example_en: The new formulation of the paint dries faster.
example_zh: 这种油漆的新配方干得更快。

definition_en: a wall, tower or other structure built to defend a place
example_en: The city's old fortifications still stand on the hill.
example_zh: 这座城市古老的防御工事仍然矗立在山上。

definition_en: a large, strong building or place built for defense
example_en: The fortress protected the harbor from attack.
example_zh: 这座堡垒保护港口免受攻击。

definition_en: the process by which remains of living things turn into fossils
example_en: Fossilization usually requires quick burial in mud or sand.
example_zh: 形成化石通常需要遗体被泥沙迅速掩埋。

definition_en: to encourage something to develop
example_en: The club fosters a love of reading among children.
example_zh: 这个俱乐部培养孩子们对阅读的热爱。

definition_en: forming the base from which everything else develops
example_en: Counting is a foundational skill in mathematics.
example_zh: 数数是数学中的一项基础技能。

definition_en: a small piece broken off from something larger
example_en: Fragments of pottery were found in the cave.
example_zh: 洞穴里发现了陶器碎片。

definition_en: weak and easily damaged or broken
example_en: The frail bridge shook in the wind.
example_zh: 那座不结实的桥在风中摇晃。

definition_en: a set of ideas or rules used as a basis for understanding or deciding something
example_en: The theory offers a useful framework for studying cities.
example_zh: 这个理论为研究城市提供了有用的框架。

definition_en: the force that slows surfaces rubbing together; also, difficulty or resistance
example_en: Long forms add friction to online shopping.
example_zh: 冗长的表格给网上购物增添了阻碍。

definition_en: the edge of settled land, next to wild country; a border
example_en: The family moved west to the frontier in the 1870s.
example_zh: 这家人在 19 世纪 70 年代西迁到了边疆。

definition_en: lasting only a short time and hard to keep track of; (n.) a person who is running away
definition_zh: 转瞬即逝的；流散的；逃亡者
example_en: Old newspapers preserve fugitive poems that were never collected in books.
example_zh: 旧报纸保存了一些从未结集出版的零散诗作。

definition_en: the range of things that something can do; usefulness
example_en: The update adds new functionality to the app.
example_zh: 这次更新给应用增加了新功能。

definition_en: relating to or caused by fungi such as mushrooms and molds
example_en: The tree died of a fungal disease.
example_zh: 这棵树死于真菌病害。

definition_en: the quality of being exchangeable for another item of the same kind
example_en: The fungibility of money means one dollar is as good as any other.
example_zh: 货币的可互换性意味着任何一美元都是等值的。

definition_en: an enclosed space where a very hot fire heats metal, clay or a building
example_en: The glass is melted in a furnace.
example_zh: 玻璃是在熔炉里熔化的。

definition_en: in addition to what has just been said
example_en: The plan is too expensive; furthermore, it would take years.
example_zh: 这个计划太贵了；而且要花好几年。

definition_en: to join together to form a single thing, often by melting
example_en: Heat causes the two layers to fuse.
example_zh: 热量使这两层熔合在一起。

definition_en: to give a lot of attention or worry to someone or something
example_en: The aunts fussed over the new baby all afternoon.
example_zh: 姑姑们整个下午都围着新生儿转。

definition_en: to collect or gain something such as praise or support
example_en: The film garnered five awards.
example_zh: 这部电影获得了五个奖项。

definition_en: general and not specific; shared by a whole group
example_en: The advice was too generic to be useful.
example_zh: 这些建议太笼统，没什么用。

definition_en: the complete set of genetic information in a living thing
example_en: Scientists have mapped the entire human genome.
example_zh: 科学家已经绘制出完整的人类基因组图谱。

definition_en: a particular type of art, writing, music or film
example_en: Science fiction is her favorite genre.
example_zh: 科幻是她最喜欢的类型。

definition_en: real; sincere; not fake
example_en: The signature was proved to be genuine.
example_zh: 签名被证明是真的。

definition_en: really; truly
example_en: She was genuinely surprised by the gift.
example_zh: 收到礼物她是真的很惊讶。

definition_en: to add information to a photo or online post that shows the place where it was made
example_en: She geotagged her photos so friends could see where she had traveled.
example_zh: 她给照片加了地理位置标记，好让朋友们看到她去过哪些地方。

definition_en: (gird up) to prepare yourself for something difficult
example_en: The team girded itself for a difficult final match.
example_zh: 球队为艰难的决赛做好了准备。

definition_en: a thin shiny coating on pottery; to cover with such a coating
example_en: The potter chose a blue glaze for the vase.
example_zh: 陶工给花瓶选了蓝色的釉。

definition_en: to shine softly
example_en: The wet street gleamed under the lamps.
example_zh: 湿漉漉的街道在路灯下泛着光。

definition_en: a quick or brief look at something
example_en: The old diary offers a glimpse of life in the 1800s.
example_zh: 这本旧日记让人得以一窥 19 世纪的生活。

definition_en: to control or guide how something works or behaves
example_en: Strict rules govern the use of the laboratory.
example_zh: 实验室的使用有严格的规定。

definition_en: the way an organization or country is managed and controlled
example_en: Workers have a say in the company's governance.
example_zh: 工人在公司治理上有发言权。

definition_en: a soft black form of carbon used in pencils
example_en: Pencil "lead" is actually made of graphite.
example_zh: 铅笔的“铅芯”其实是石墨做的。

definition_en: giving pleasure or satisfaction
definition_zh: 令人欣慰的；令人满足的
example_en: It is gratifying to see former students succeed.
example_zh: 看到以前的学生有所成就，令人欣慰。

definition_en: the feeling of being thankful
example_en: She wrote a letter to express her gratitude.
example_zh: 她写了一封信表达感激之情。

definition_en: to be attracted to and move toward something
example_en: Young readers gravitate toward adventure stories.
example_zh: 年轻读者往往喜欢冒险故事。

definition_en: a flat, heavy pan or plate used for cooking over heat
example_en: She cooked flatbread on a hot griddle.
example_zh: 她在烧热的平底烤盘上烙饼。

definition_en: deep sadness, especially after someone dies
example_en: He was overcome with grief at the news.
example_zh: 听到消息，他悲痛不已。

definition_en: very serious and causing great pain or harm
example_en: The general made a grievous mistake.
example_zh: 将军犯了一个严重的错误。

definition_en: (of animals) to clean the fur or skin of itself or another animal
example_en: Monkeys groom each other to build friendships.
example_zh: 猴子互相梳理毛发来增进关系。

definition_en: new and very important; doing something never done before
example_en: Her groundbreaking research changed the field.
example_zh: 她开创性的研究改变了这个领域。

definition_en: water that is found under the ground in soil and rock
example_en: Many villages depend on groundwater from wells.
example_zh: 许多村庄靠井里的地下水生活。

definition_en: early work that prepares the way for later success
example_en: Early experiments laid the groundwork for the discovery.
example_zh: 早期的实验为这项发现打下了基础。

definition_en: too ready to believe what other people say; easily tricked
example_en: He is so gullible that he believes every advertisement.
example_zh: 他太容易轻信了，什么广告都相信。

definition_en: used to something because of repeated experience
example_en: City birds become habituated to traffic noise.
example_zh: 城市里的鸟逐渐习惯了交通噪音。

definition_en: used so often that it is no longer interesting or original
example_en: "Happily ever after" is a hackneyed ending.
example_zh: “从此过上了幸福的生活”是老套的结局。

definition_en: (Hawaiian) a traditional Hawaiian house with a thatched roof
example_en: The builder taught students how to raise a hale.
example_zh: 这位建造者教学生们怎样搭建夏威夷传统茅草屋。

definition_en: a sign that something is going to happen soon
example_en: The first warm wind is a harbinger of spring.
example_zh: 第一阵暖风是春天的预兆。

definition_en: sounding pleasant together; peaceful and well matched
example_en: The choir produced a rich, harmonious sound.
example_zh: 合唱团的歌声饱满而和谐。

definition_en: to control and use the power of something
example_en: Engineers harness the wind to produce electricity.
example_zh: 工程师利用风力发电。

definition_en: severe and unpleasant; difficult to live in
example_en: Few plants survive the harsh desert climate.
example_zh: 很少有植物能在严酷的沙漠气候中存活。

definition_en: (old use) has
example_en: "He hath spoken" means "he has spoken."
example_zh: “He hath spoken”就是“he has spoken”的意思。

definition_en: behaving as if you are better than other people
example_en: The haughty prince refused to speak to the servants.
example_zh: 傲慢的王子不肯跟仆人说话。

definition_en: dangerous, especially to health or safety
example_en: Workers wear masks when handling hazardous chemicals.
example_zh: 工人处理危险化学品时要戴口罩。

definition_en: the quality of being unclear or not exact
example_en: The haziness of the rule led to arguments.
example_zh: 这条规定含糊不清，引起了争论。

definition_en: not clear; vague
example_en: I have only a hazy memory of that day.
example_zh: 我对那天只有模糊的记忆。

definition_en: to make a feeling or effect stronger
example_en: Music is used to heighten the tension in the film.
example_zh: 影片用音乐来增强紧张感。

definition_en: the outer boundary of the region of space affected by the Sun's wind
definition_zh: 日球层顶（太阳风影响范围的外边界）
example_en: The spacecraft crossed the heliopause and entered interstellar space.
example_zh: 探测器越过日球层顶，进入了星际空间。

definition_en: one half of Earth, such as the northern or southern half
example_en: Summer in the southern hemisphere begins in December.
example_zh: 南半球的夏天从十二月开始。

definition_en: from this time on
example_en: Henceforth, all visitors must sign in at the desk.
example_zh: 从今以后，所有访客都必须在前台登记。

definition_en: made up of many different kinds of things
definition_zh: 由不同成分组成的；混杂的
example_en: The city has a heterogeneous population from many countries.
example_zh: 这座城市的人口来自许多国家，构成多样。

definition_en: using a simple rule or practical shortcut to solve a problem
example_en: "Buy the cheapest one" is a simple heuristic for shoppers.
example_zh: “买最便宜的”是购物者的一条简单经验法则。

definition_en: a pause or break in an activity
example_en: The show returned after a two-year hiatus.
example_zh: 这个节目中断两年后回归了。

definition_en: arranged in levels of importance or rank
example_en: The army has a strict hierarchical structure.
example_zh: 军队有严格的等级结构。

definition_en: a system in which people or things are ranked one above another
example_en: He rose quickly through the company hierarchy.
example_zh: 他在公司层级中晋升得很快。

definition_en: a picture or symbol used in ancient Egyptian writing
example_en: The walls of the tomb are covered with hieroglyphs.
example_zh: 墓室的墙上布满了象形文字。

definition_en: joined by a part that lets it swing open and closed, like a door
example_en: The box has a hinged lid.
example_zh: 这个盒子的盖子是带铰链的。

definition_en: the writing of history, and the study of how history is written
example_en: Recent historiography pays more attention to ordinary people.
example_zh: 近年来的史学更加关注普通人。

definition_en: until now or until that time
example_en: The team found a hitherto unknown species of frog.
example_zh: 团队发现了一种此前不为人知的青蛙。

definition_en: a hidden store of valuable things; to collect and hide things
example_en: A farmer found a hoard of Roman coins in his field.
example_zh: 一位农民在自家地里发现了一批窖藏的罗马钱币。

definition_en: a low or sunken place in the ground; empty inside
example_en: Rain collected in the hollows of the field.
example_zh: 雨水积在田里的洼地中。

definition_en: the state of being all the same or all of one kind
example_en: The homogeneity of the houses made the street look dull.
example_zh: 房子全都一个样，让这条街显得单调。

definition_en: unfriendly or angry feeling or behavior
example_en: There was open hostility between the two teams.
example_zh: 两支队伍之间公然敌对。

definition_en: a color or a shade of a color (hued, adj.: colored)
example_en: The sky turned a soft pink hue at sunset.
example_zh: 日落时天空变成了柔和的粉色。

definition_en: the amount of water in the air
example_en: High humidity makes hot days feel even hotter.
example_zh: 湿度大会让热天感觉更热。

definition_en: to remove the dry outer covering of grain or seeds; the covering itself
example_en: The villagers husked the rice by hand.
example_zh: 村民们用手给稻谷脱壳。

definition_en: made by combining two different things; a mixture of two kinds
example_en: The car has a hybrid engine that uses gas and electricity.
example_zh: 这辆车装的是油电混合动力发动机。

definition_en: to breed two different kinds of plant or animal together
example_en: Farmers hybridized two kinds of corn to get a stronger plant.
example_zh: 农民把两种玉米杂交，培育出更强壮的植株。

definition_en: relating to water or other liquid moving through pipes or channels
example_en: The dam is a great work of hydraulic engineering.
example_zh: 这座大坝是水利工程的杰作。

definition_en: relating to the movement and distribution of water on Earth
example_en: Heavy logging changed the hydrological cycle of the valley.
example_zh: 大量伐木改变了山谷的水文循环。

definition_en: a scientist who studies water on and under Earth's surface
example_en: The hydrologist measured the river's flow each month.
example_zh: 水文学家每个月测量这条河的流量。

definition_en: a religious song of praise
example_en: The choir sang a hymn at the start of the service.
example_zh: 仪式开始时唱诗班唱了一首赞美诗。

definition_en: text on a screen that contains links to other text
example_en: Web pages are written in hypertext, so one click leads to another page.
example_zh: 网页是用超文本写成的，点一下就能跳到另一页。

definition_en: to suggest a possible explanation that has not yet been proved
example_en: Scientists hypothesize that the lake was once much larger.
example_zh: 科学家推测这个湖以前要大得多。

definition_en: a unit of poetic rhythm with one weak syllable followed by one strong syllable
definition_zh: 抑扬格（一轻一重的音步）
example_en: The word "begin" is an iamb: be-GIN.
example_zh: “begin”这个词是抑扬格：先轻后重。

definition_en: widely known and admired as a symbol of something
example_en: The tower is the city's most iconic building.
example_zh: 这座塔是这座城市最具标志性的建筑。

definition_en: unusual and particular to one person or thing
example_en: The writer has an idiosyncratic way of using commas.
example_zh: 这位作家使用逗号的方式很独特。

definition_en: a large lizard that lives in warm regions
example_en: An iguana lay in the sun on a warm rock.
example_zh: 一只鬣蜥趴在温暖的岩石上晒太阳。

definition_en: to light something up; to make something clearer
example_en: The letters illuminate the poet's early life.
example_zh: 这些信件让人更了解诗人的早年生活。

definition_en: pictures, or language that creates pictures in the reader's mind
example_en: The poem is full of imagery of the sea.
example_zh: 这首诗充满了关于大海的意象。

definition_en: a situation in which two things are not equal or evenly spread
example_en: An imbalance in air pressure caused the door to slam.
example_zh: 气压不平衡导致门砰地关上。

definition_en: a copy of something; the act of copying
example_en: Children learn many words through imitation.
example_zh: 孩子们通过模仿学会许多词。

definition_en: a person who copies the work or behavior of another
example_en: The singer's success produced many imitators.
example_zh: 这位歌手成功之后出现了许多模仿者。

definition_en: about to happen very soon
example_en: Dark clouds warned of an imminent storm.
example_zh: 乌云预示着暴风雨即将来临。

definition_en: to give a quality, feeling or piece of information to someone or something
example_en: The spice imparts a warm flavor to the soup.
example_zh: 这种香料给汤增添了一种温暖的味道。

definition_en: treating all sides fairly; not favoring anyone
example_en: A judge must remain impartial.
example_zh: 法官必须保持公正。

definition_en: a measure of how much something resists the flow of sound or electric energy
example_en: The ear matches the impedance of air to that of the fluid inside it.
example_zh: 耳朵能让空气的阻抗与耳内液体的阻抗相匹配。

definition_en: to slow down or block the progress of something
example_en: Fallen trees impeded the rescue team.
example_zh: 倒下的树木阻碍了救援队前进。

definition_en: a command; (adj.) extremely important and urgent
example_en: "Sit down!" is an imperative.
example_zh: “坐下！”是一句祈使句。

definition_en: relating to an empire or its ruler
example_en: The city was once an imperial capital.
example_zh: 这座城市曾是帝国的都城。

definition_en: something that makes a process begin or happen faster
example_en: The discovery gave new impetus to the search for a cure.
example_zh: 这一发现为寻找治疗方法提供了新的动力。

definition_en: to put a plan into action; (n.) a tool
example_en: The school will implement the new policy next year.
example_zh: 学校明年将实施这项新政策。

definition_en: the act of putting a plan or system into use
example_en: Implementation of the plan was delayed by a lack of funds.
example_zh: 由于缺少资金，计划的实施被推迟了。

definition_en: a possible effect or result; something suggested without being said
example_en: The discovery has important implications for medicine.
example_zh: 这项发现对医学有重要意义。
